style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: minimalist studio composition of a modular mechanical assembly on a real brushed steel surface, asymmetrical off-centre layout. Two recognisable engineered parts: an elaborate, premium white ceramic watch casing shell, and a small, utilitarian rectangular battery module unlatched and resting beside it. Hard clean edges, one directional key light throwing a long cast shadow across the weathered steel, matte muted modern palette, generous negative space, no text, no moulded lettering.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, typography, watermarks, UI, printed labels
rationale: This treatment distills the economic trap of the device into its physical reality: two distinct parts (the cheap consumable and the expensive shell) whose artificial pairing dictates the total cost of ownership. Nano Banana constructs this cleanly as a deliberate mechanical arrangement.
cue: set by the case you bought
subject: a premium ceramic watch casing shell and a basic battery module
core_thesis: The cheapest part in a watch is the one that ends its life, and the price of reaching it is set by the case you bought, not by the part that failed.
core_conflict: Consumable component replacement cost vs. premium outer casing pricing tiers
